sentences.text: The genus name translates to 'air thief' due to hollow spaces within the bones filled with air sacs.
An L-shaped shoulder structure identifies this animal as a member of the Paraves group, which includes dromaeosaurids, troodontids, and birds.
Based on the shoulder bone size, this creature was roughly three times smaller than Velociraptor.
Scientists know the animal only from a single complete left shoulder girdle.
The species was named Pneumatoraptor fodori to honor Géza Fodor, who funded the excavation.
The holotype specimen, cataloged as MTM V.2008.38.1, is currently housed at the Hungarian Natural History Museum in Budapest.
Pneumatoraptor is classified as a small paravian dinosaur, possibly belonging to the dromaeosaurid family.
Although the remains are too incomplete to definitively place it in a specific subgroup, many bone features are similar to dromaeosaurids.
Pneumatoraptor lived during the Santonian age of the late Cretaceous period, approximately 85 million years ago.
The fossil record for this taxon spans from 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago.
